text:
micah: noticing repeated SLO misses on p99 for text-generation routes in us-west-2 since ~08:30 UTC. p50/p90 ok, p99 spikes to 1.6s from 800ms. sounds like continuous batching pressure and max_batch truncation on certain shards. :frowning:
anya: seeing the same. dashboard shows one GPU host group at 92% runqueue while others are ~45%.
rajiv: are we sure it's not a slow model variant? which model config?
micah: primarily gptx-4-llama (v2) with max_sequence ~2048. busy tenants have long contexts + streaming so the batcher ends up holding small batches because max_batch is hit frequently by long requests, leading to queueing.
marta: infra-bot posted alerts: 
```
ALERT: shard-hot-queueing us-west-2-gpupool-7
metric: runqueue_length > 80% for 4m
affected: hosts 7a,7b,7c
```
micah: logs show repeated admission rejections with reason=MAX_BATCH_HIT. snippet: `admission=[accept] size=8 but max_batch=8 -> immediate flush; new reqs queued`. So throughput OK but latency increases because long-seq requests prevent effective packing.
anya: interesting — so small batches get flushed early and we can't pack short requests behind long ones. packing policy is naive FIFO per-shard.
rajiv: can we confirm it's per-shard routing causing hotspots? maybe the smart-router hash maps user->shard and a few customers are heavy.
marta: I pulled routing logs: top 3 tenant-ids account for 38% of requests to shard 7 over last 30m. they have long-prefill patterns.
micah: proposed short-term mitigations:
- reduce `max_batch` on shard 7 to 4 to avoid large batch waits for long sequences (tradeoff: throughput drop)
- enable `hot_client_isolation` so heavy tenants get their own admission queue
- bump autoscaler floor for us-west-2 by +2 GPUs to relieve pressure (costy)
anya: also consider per-request `max_tokens` cap enforcement at API layer for tenants hitting >1500 tokens frequently. that is policy-y but immediate.
rajiv: long-term: change batch admission to age-priority + size-aware packing: let smaller requests skip ahead if a head-of-queue request has been delayed > X ms. or implement speculative splitting of long requests into prefix+suffix for faster front-loading.
marta: also a cheap change: introduce a per-shard token-bucket rate limiter that accounts for estimated token consumption (tokens/request * concurrency) so we don't oversubscribe a shard.
micah: agree. which of these can we flip in next 30m?
anya: I can lower max_batch to 4 and enable hot_client_isolation on shard 7 now. will monitor.
rajiv: I'll prototype the age-priority admission change in a branch, but can't roll in 30m.
marta: I'll open a quick autoscaler ticket for a +2 instance noop scale to be ready if lowering max_batch causes throughput issues: TKT-4531.
infra-bot: deploybot: starting canary for config-change `eng-runtime/max_batch_override/shard-7` by anya at 1780154370
anya: rolled to 3 hosts in shard-7 canary. metrics in 2m.
micah: thanks. follow-ups:
- if p99 doesn't drop in 10m, we flip autoscale +2.
- create an incident doc if error budget hits 5% threshold.
- rajiv to draft admission algorithm PR, marta to spec token-bucket limiter.
rajiv: noted. will post design doc in #eng-runtime/infra later today.
marta: cost note: +2 GPUs in us-west-2 ~ $3k/mo. if we keep that permanently we need a business case.
micah: add to runbook: detect hot-shard by >60% of traffic from top-3 tenants and runqueue length >80% for 5min -> apply `hot_client_isolation` + temporary max_batch downscale.
anya: initial metrics: after canary, p99 fell to 980ms on canary hosts, overall cluster p99 down to ~1.1s (was 1.6s). continuing rollout.
marta: good. capture exact metric windows and save dashboard.
micah: awesome. capture action items and close once rollout done + autoscale decision. :thumbsup:
